mixed3a:136.CP_s1: The unit responds to a fine, granular or stippled surface texture (asphalt, carpet, knit fabric, reptile or insect scales, fruit skin) that sits just below a horizontal boundary with a smoother or darker region above it, like the ground under an object.
mixed3a:136.CP_s2: The unit responds to a fine, granular or stippled surface texture, such as asphalt, carpet, gravel, reptile or insect scales, woven fabric or fruit rind, filling the lower part of its field with a different, smoother region or object edge just above it. In effect it detects textured ground or surface meeting an occluding boundary from below.
mixed3a:136.CP_s3: Responds to fine, dense, granular or speckled surface texture (asphalt, gravel, carpet, woven fabric, scaly or pitted skin), typically filling the lower part of the receptive field below a smoother or darker region, i.e. a horizontal boundary with texture underneath.
mixed3a:136.CPA_s1: The unit responds to fine, granular or speckled surface texture (asphalt, fabric weave, scaly skin, fruit rind, fur), especially when a horizontal-ish boundary sits above it with the textured region filling the lower part of the patch.
mixed3a:136.CPA_s2: The unit responds to a fine-grained granular or speckled surface texture (asphalt, carpet, fabric weave, scaly or bumpy skin, fruit rind) with a smooth or darker object edge lying above it, so the texture fills the lower part of the patch under a boundary.
mixed3a:136.CPA_s3: The unit responds to fine-grained granular or speckled texture (asphalt, carpet, fabric weave, scaly or pitted skin, foliage) in the lower part of the receptive field, typically just below a horizontal edge where a darker or different-textured region sits above it.

mixed3a:110.CP_s1: The unit responds to a vertical border where a smooth, uniform surface on the left meets a fine, high-contrast dotted or granular texture on the right, such as knit, polka dots, speaker grilles, keypads, QR codes, or thatch.
mixed3a:110.CP_s2: The unit responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine dotted, granular or perforated texture on the right, such as a knit edge, a speaker grille, polka dots, sequins or a thatch edge.
mixed3a:110.CP_s3: Responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine, repeated dot-like texture on the right, such as polka dots, knit stitches, perforations, studs or speckles.
mixed3a:110.CPA_s1: The unit detects a vertical boundary with a smooth, uniform region on the left and a fine, repeated dotted or granular texture on the right, such as a knit, perforations, polka dots, a QR code or thatch.
mixed3a:110.CPA_s2: The unit responds to a vertical-ish boundary with a smooth, uniform region on the left and a fine, high-density repeating texture (dots, knit, perforations, sequins, printed patterns) on the right.
mixed3a:110.CPA_s3: The unit responds to a vertical-ish boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine, high-density texture of dots, knits, perforations or speckles on the right.

mixed3b:379.CP_s1: The unit detects the upper-left curved rim of a circular object, i.e. a convex arc bending from up-left over to the right, most strongly on watch, compass and gauge dials. It extends more weakly to other circular rims (colanders, plaques, shields, mirrors) and to non-dial arcs such as bridge arches, painted rainbow stripes and bent railings.
mixed3b:379.CP_s2: Detects the curved rim of a circular object, an arc boundary seen from inside the disc, usually its upper-left edge; this is strongest on watch, compass and gauge dials. It also responds more weakly to other curved arcs such as plaque edges, bowl rims, bridge arches, logo stripes and bent railings.
mixed3b:379.CP_s3: The unit detects the upper-left curved rim of a circular object, an arc boundary with concentric bands; it fires most on dial faces such as watches, compasses, gauges and clock faces.
mixed3b:379.CPA_s1: The unit detects the upper curved rim/bezel of a circular object, typically a convex arc running across the top of the receptive field. It fires most for watch, compass and gauge dial edges, and more weakly for other arcs such as bridge arches, bowl rims and handrails.
mixed3b:379.CPA_s2: The unit detects the upper-left arc of a circular rim or bezel: a curved boundary bending from roughly vertical on the left toward horizontal at the top, as on watch faces, compasses, gauges, plaques and round signs.
mixed3b:379.CPA_s3: Responds to the upper-left arc of a circular rim or bezel, a curved boundary concave toward the lower right such as the edge of a watch face, compass, dial or gauge, curved more strongly than a straight edge.

mixed4b:237.CP_s1: The unit responds to the side windows of road vehicles: the glass of a car, truck or van door seen from the side, with the window frame, pillars and often the side mirror.
mixed4b:237.CP_s2: The unit responds to vehicle side windows and cab doors: the upright window frame or pillar on a car, truck, van or cab door, seen from the side.
mixed4b:237.CP_s3: The unit responds to the side window and door region of vehicle cabins (cars, trucks, vans), specifically the upright window frame with its pillar and the door edge beneath it.
mixed4b:237.CPA_s1: The unit responds to the side windows and door-window frame of motor vehicles (cars, trucks, vans, ambulances, taxis), in particular the cab or front-door window with its pillar and window frame seen from the side.
mixed4b:237.CPA_s2: The unit responds to the side windows and doors of road vehicles (cars, pickups, vans, trucks): glass window panes framed by door pillars and the door edge, seen upright.
mixed4b:237.CPA_s3: The unit responds to the side window and door area of road vehicles: the glass window pane framed by the door/cab pillar on cars, pickups, vans and trucks.

mixed4b:373.CP_s1: The unit responds to a vehicle's front wheel, seen from the side, sitting inside its arched wheel well. It responds to this across cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines.
mixed4b:373.CP_s2: The unit responds to the front wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side: a round tyre and hub set under the curved arch of the wheel well. It responds the same way to cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines.
mixed4b:373.CP_s3: The unit detects vehicle wheels seen from the side together with the wheel arch or fender above them. It is most active on the front wheel of cars, trucks, buses and emergency vehicles.
mixed4b:373.CPA_s1: The unit detects vehicle wheels set in their wheel arches, meaning a tire or rim under the curved fender edge of the body, on cars, trucks, buses and fire engines, viewed upright from the side.
mixed4b:373.CPA_s2: The unit detects the wheel of a road vehicle together with the arch above it, which is usually a front wheel seen from the side with the curved fender over the tyre, on cars, trucks, buses and emergency vehicles.
mixed4b:373.CPA_s3: Detects the front wheel of a road vehicle together with the arched wheel well above it, shown in upright side view: a dark round tire beneath the curved fender edge. It fires the same way for cars, trucks, buses, vans and fire engines.

mixed4b:431.CP_s1: Responds to the fur-covered side of the head and neck of animals facing right, the cheek, ear and neck region just behind the face, mostly dogs. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals like monkeys, hyenas, hamsters, squirrels and mink.
mixed4b:431.CP_s2: Responds to furry mammal heads and the fur near them, mostly dogs, at the side of the face, cheek and ear, where furred head meets neck or background; it extends more weakly to other furry mammals (dhole, hyena, monkeys, hamster, squirrel, mink).
mixed4b:431.CP_s3: The unit responds to furry mammal heads and faces in their usual upright, side-on pose, most of all dogs. The red boxes usually fall on the side of the head, cheek or ear area. It responds more weakly to related furry animals such as a dhole, hyena, monkeys, hamster, squirrel and mink.
mixed4b:431.CPA_s1: Responds to the furry cheek, ear and neck area of a mammal's head, mostly dogs. It prefers animals facing or turned to the right, and also fires more weakly on other furry mammals such as monkeys, a hyena, a hamster, a squirrel and a mink.
mixed4b:431.CPA_s2: The unit responds to the furry neck, shoulder or cheek of a mammal, mostly dogs, when the animal's head is turned toward the right of the image. It responds more weakly to other furry mammals such as monkeys, a hyena, a hamster, a squirrel and a mink in the same pose.
mixed4b:431.CPA_s3: The unit responds to the furry cheek, ear and neck region of a mammal head, mostly dogs, and prefers heads turned or facing toward the right of the image.

mixed4b:443.CP_s1: The unit detects upright canid faces, firing most strongly on the region around the eye and upper muzzle of dogs, and somewhat less on wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.CP_s2: Responds to upright canine faces, most strongly to the eye and upper muzzle of dogs looking toward the camera. It extends more weakly to closely related canids such as wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.CP_s3: The unit detects the upright face of a dog, centered on the eye region and the side of the muzzle, and also responds more weakly to the faces of similar canids such as foxes and wolves.
mixed4b:443.CPA_s1: Responds to upright canine faces (dogs, wolves, foxes), peaking around the eye/upper-face region of a frontal or three-quarter face, with weaker responses to other mammal faces such as monkeys, mink and bears.
mixed4b:443.CPA_s2: Responds to upright, front-facing canine faces, most strongly in the region around the eye and the bridge of the snout. The response extends more weakly to similar faces of other furry mammals such as foxes, wolves, monkeys and bears.
mixed4b:443.CPA_s3: Responds to upright canid faces (dogs, plus wolves and foxes), firing most strongly on the eye region beside the muzzle. It responds more weakly to other mammal faces such as monkeys, a mink and a bear.

mixed4d:409.CP_s1: The unit responds to upright, side-on views of the body or flank of four-legged animals, mostly dogs (plus one weasel), and separately to the side of cars and trucks at wheel and door level. Both depend on a horizontal body above ground-contact legs or wheels.
mixed4d:409.CP_s2: The unit responds to the side-on profile of an upright, horizontally elongated body held up by supports underneath, such as a standing dog's flank over its legs or a car's body over its wheels. It appears to encode this configural shape rather than any object category.
mixed4d:409.CP_s3: The unit responds to the side profile of a horizontally elongated body held up off the ground on legs or wheels, at mid-body. This covers standing dogs (and a weasel) seen from the side as well as cars, trucks and vans seen from the side.
mixed4d:409.CPA_s1: The unit responds to the side-view body of an elongated object held upright above the ground on legs or wheels, mainly dogs (and a stoat) and cars or vans seen in profile; the red box sits on the flank or the lower body above the supports.
mixed4d:409.CPA_s2: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body seen side-on and standing on supports below it: the flank of a standing four-legged animal (mostly dogs, also a weasel) or a car or truck body above its wheels.
mixed4d:409.CPA_s3: The unit responds to the side-profile view of a horizontally elongated body resting on legs or wheels. This covers the flank of a standing quadruped (mostly dogs, also a stoat) and the side or lower body of a car or truck near the wheels.

mixed4e:55.CP_s1: Responds to the lower-middle face of furry mammals (the muzzle, nose and whisker region just below the eyes), most strongly on cats, foxes and red pandas, with weaker extensions to similar face-like regions on other animals such as dogs, hamsters and a stork's cheek.
mixed4e:55.CP_s2: Responds to the lower face/muzzle of upright furry mammals, mainly cats, foxes, red pandas and lynxes: the area around the nose, mouth and whiskers where light fur meets darker fur. Weaker responses come from similar face-like patterns, such as a stork's white head with a dark eye near the beak and the front grille/headlight of a red car.
mixed4e:55.CP_s3: Responds to the muzzle/snout region of upright furry animal faces (fox, red panda, cat, hamster, lynx, dog), especially the area just below and between the eyes around the nose, with whiskers and fur. Weaker extensions to other face-like structures with similar layout, like a stork's eye and beak base and a car's grille and headlight front.
mixed4e:55.CPA_s1: The unit responds to the upright lower face of furry mammals (fox, red panda, cat, lynx, hamster): the muzzle, nose and mouth area below the eyes, where light fur meets darker fur or the nose. Weaker responses go to similar face-like regions on other things, such as a car's front grille and a stork's face.
mixed4e:55.CPA_s2: Responds to the lower-central face of upright furry mammals, centered on the muzzle, nose and whisker pad. Fox, red panda, cat and lynx faces dominate, and the response is strongest for that face in its normal upright orientation.
mixed4e:55.CPA_s3: The unit responds to the lower-central face of upright furry animals: the muzzle, nose and whisker region of cats, foxes, red pandas, lynxes and dogs, with the face pointing up. It responds weakly to similar shapes such as a car grille or front (#6) and a stork's face (#20).

mixed5a:719.CP_s1: The unit responds mainly to close-up shots of handmade or manufactured objects with decorative, ornamented surfaces, such as embroidered or printed fabric, embossed metal or clay, crochet, and floral motifs. It responds more weakly to the smooth, rounded contours of plain manufactured objects such as a mouse, shoes, knee pads and a revolver.
mixed5a:719.CP_s2: The unit responds mainly to rounded, curved contours on close-up handcrafted or manufactured objects, such as the bulging edge of a mouse, shoe toe, knee pad, stocking or teapot. A weaker extension covers ornate radial or floral surface patterns like rosettes, brooches and the manhole design.
mixed5a:719.CP_s3: The unit mainly responds to curved, outlined contours on man-made objects, especially rounded edges of smooth or embossed surfaces such as a mouse, armour, knee pads, shoes and a teapot. It extends more weakly to decorative motifs on crafted or fabric items, like floral or radial patterns, stockings, crochet and a flag.
mixed5a:719.CPA_s1: The unit responds to close-up, product-style views of man-made objects, especially crafted or decorated surfaces such as fabric, embroidery, ornamental motifs, molded plastic or leather, with their curved contours and edges. Weaker responses extend to similar decorated-looking natural items such as flowers.
mixed5a:719.CPA_s2: The unit responds to the surfaces of handcrafted or manufactured objects that carry decorative motifs, such as floral or ornamental prints, embroidery, crochet, embossing and printed fabric. A weaker extension covers smooth, curved, glossy man-made surfaces with raised contours, such as a computer mouse, armour, knee pads and a toy gun.
mixed5a:719.CPA_s3: Responds to close-up surfaces of small man-made or handcrafted objects, especially decorated or patterned ones such as embossed or printed motifs, appliqué fabric, crochet and ornamental flowers, with a weaker response to plain glossy black manufactured items (mouse, knee pads, toy gun).
